solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Disappear, having run out of polish (6)

indicators.note: something that has run out of a place has left it, so R, for run, leaves the word it names

blocks.note: a polish or glossy coating for wood
R = run, the cricket scoring abbreviation; it is removed

annotation.surface: A shoe-shiner's tin runs dry and they make themselves scarce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run out of' reads as one phrase meaning exhausted, but split it: R for run, taken out of VARNISH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to go out of sight, the way a magician's coin does.

entries.clue: Writer almost published following potential difference (8)

indicators.note: almost there means not quite complete, so the word stops one letter short
what follows comes after, so the published piece is placed after the potential difference

blocks.note: the volt is the unit of potential difference
AIRED = published, broadcast; 'almost' drops the D

annotation.surface: A physics paper nearly makes it into print after a circuit experiment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Potential difference' looks like vague talk of rivalry, but it is the physicist's name for voltage.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the pen name of François-Marie Arouet, the French Enlightenment author of Candide, stands for writers in general.

entries.clue: After heading off, hitch horse (3)

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter, and with the heading off the word is decapitated

blocks.note: a hitch in the sense of a problem or obstacle; drop the first letter S

annotation.surface: Once you've set out, harness the horse to the cart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hitch horse' reads as harnessing, but hitch is a noun here: a snag, which loses its S to leave NAG.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a sneer: a nag is an old or worn-out horse, but any horse can be called one.

entries.clue: Mass rally begins with it (7)

blocks.note: the Catholic Eucharist, a form of church worship
in tennis, the shot that puts the ball in play before any exchange of strokes

annotation.surface: A political rally is opened with a big public act of worship.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a crowd at a political rally; the second half is a cryptic hint pointing at tennis, where every rally opens with a service.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a Mass is a form of religious service, and a tennis rally starts with the serve, also called the service.

entries.clue: Ambassador travels by horse around British Isles (8)

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so the ambassador riding encloses the British letter

blocks.note: HE = His Excellency, an ambassador's title
B = British
to go on horseback

annotation.surface: A diplomat tours the British Isles on horseback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'British Isles' is a phrase you read as one, but British is only B and Isles is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Hebrides are a group of islands off the west coast of Scotland.

entries.clue: 1D made KP nuts, a canned product (10,4)

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, and letters gone crazy are thrown out of order

blocks.note: 1 down is VOLTAIRE; with MADE and KP, 14 letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Voltaire turns up in a snack factory producing KP nuts in tins.
annotation.walkthrough: KP is a British brand of peanuts, so 'KP nuts' looks like a product; here KP is two letters and nuts is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: milk concentrated by heating is sold in tins, one of many things that are canned.

entries.clue: Managed Oscar, famously said to have lost control (3,4)

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the name gives only its sound

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
the famous Oscar is the Irish playwright Oscar Wilde

annotation.surface: Oscar Wilde's legendary wit is recalled in a story of lost self-control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Famously said' seems to introduce one of Wilde's quips; it only tells you to hear his surname.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: children or weeds that run wild have got out of control.

entries.clue: Ed’s third hit stirred up gossip (not in a good way) (4,3,4)

indicators.note: whatever is stirred up is mixed around, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: 11 letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A singer called Ed releases a third hit record and it causes nasty chatter.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracket is part of the definition: it narrows gossip to the malicious kind.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to dish the dirt is to spread scandal about someone, gossip meant to harm.

entries.clue: Birdies, pars, eagles going round few and far between (6)

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, and these words surround the answer

blocks.note: birdieS PARS Eagles

annotation.surface: A golfer's good scores come round only rarely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going round' sounds like a round of golf, which is why it fits the surface so well.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things thinly scattered are few and far between.

entries.clue: The hopeless PM failing to contain the onset of inner demon (14)

indicators.note: something failing is falling apart, so the letters collapse into a new order
to contain is to hold inside, so the extra letter goes into the mix
an onset is a beginning, so take the first letter

blocks.note: 13 letters to rearrange
first letter of inner, added to the mix

annotation.surface: A failing prime minister turns out to be possessed by an inner demon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hopeless' looks like a comment on the PM, but it is part of the anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Mephistopheles is the devil to whom Faust sells his soul.

entries.clue: Such deception — Harry Lime enraged! (11)

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, and disturbed letters are moved about

blocks.note: 11 letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Harry Lime, the racketeer in the film The Third Man, flies into a rage at being tricked.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry Lime is one name in the surface; split it, and Harry becomes a verb telling you to scramble LIME ENRAGED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sleight of hand is trickery, and 'such' points back to the scrambling the clue has just done.

entries.clue: Music from eastern half of US state (3)

indicators.note: on a map east is the right, and in an across entry the right half is the end of the word

blocks.note: the largest US state; keep the right-hand three of its six letters

annotation.surface: A style of music comes from the eastern part of an American state.
annotation.walkthrough: The eastern half of Alaska is a real region, which is what hides the letter-level reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Jamaican genre that came before reggae is one kind of music.

entries.clue: Torment Scotsman bored by island hotel (7)

indicators.note: to be bored by a drill is to be pierced, so the island goes inside the Scotsman

blocks.note: Angus is a typical Scottish man's name
I = island; it goes inside ANGUS
H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A Scotsman is bored stiff by a stay at an island hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bored' suggests tedium, but here it means pierced: the island goes into Angus.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean severe mental suffering.

entries.clue: Grenoble regularly calling wanting Victor’s GPS coordinates (11)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every other letter
wanting means lacking, so the letter for Victor goes missing

blocks.note: GrEnObLe: the odd letters
a calling is a vocation
V = Victor in the phonetic alphabet; it is removed

annotation.surface: A phone call from Grenoble can't reach Victor, whose GPS position is needed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like making a phone call; it is a vocation.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose fit: the word means fixing where something is, and GPS coordinates are the result of doing so.

entries.clue: Polar explorer injected with constant drugs (7)

indicators.note: what is injected goes inside, so the constant is put into the explorer

blocks.note: Lawrence Oates, who died on Scott's Antarctic expedition
pi is the mathematical constant; it goes inside OATES

annotation.surface: An Antarctic explorer is injected with a steady supply of drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constant' reads as an adjective for the drugs; it is the noun pi.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: morphine, heroin and other opium derivatives are drugs.

entries.clue: Source of food for which we have to thank Providence? (5,6,3)

definitions.text: Source of food for which we have to thank Providence?

blocks.note: the surface reading: saying grace, thanking God for what is on the plate
the setter's reading: Providence the city, a US state capital, whose state names a farmyard bird that is a source of eggs and meat

annotation.surface: A grace said before a meal, thanking God for our food.
annotation.walkthrough: Providence with a capital letter looks like God; it is the capital of Rhode Island, where this chicken breed was developed.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the Rhode Island Red is a chicken breed that gives eggs and meat, and its home state's capital is Providence.

entries.clue: English monarch supporting dying cause (8)

indicators.note: a support holds something up from below, and in a down entry below means after

blocks.note: Eng = English
one's end is one's death
ER = Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

annotation.surface: An English king or queen lends support to a lost cause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dying cause' suggests a lost cause, but cause is the definition, split off from the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to bring something about, as poverty may give rise to crime.

entries.clue: Mass churchgoers, for example going around African capital (14)

indicators.note: something going is leaving, so the example letters depart
to go around is to encircle, so what remains wraps the capital

blocks.note: a gathering of worshippers in church
e.g. = for example; it goes, leaving CONGRATION
Lomé is the capital of Togo; CONGRATION goes around it

annotation.surface: Worshippers attend Mass in an African capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Mass beside churchgoers looks like the church service, as it did at 3 down, but here it means a heap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a jumbled collection of things gathered into one lump.

entries.clue: In Scotland, he’s paid to find the net and secure the game (7)

definitions.text: In Scotland, he’s paid to find the net and secure the game

blocks.clueFragment: find the net and secure the game
blocks.note: the surface reading: a footballer scoring and sealing the match
the setter's reading: a Highland estate worker who lands salmon in a net and retrieves the shot birds, the game

annotation.surface: A Scottish footballer is paid to score and win the match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Find the net' and 'secure the game' are football phrases; read literally they are the landing net and the shot game birds.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a ghillie is an attendant hired on Scottish estates to help at fishing and shooting.

entries.clue: Leader of archers put on his equipment, trembling (7)

indicators.note: the leader goes in front, so take the first letter
in a down entry, what is put on something sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: first letter of archers
the case an archer carries his arrows in

annotation.surface: The chief archer, shaking, puts on his gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'His equipment' ties back to the archer, and the quiver is exactly that, while also meaning a tremble.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be aquiver is to be quivering, trembling all over.

entries.clue: Sailor on the way overseas (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, a thing on another sits above it, so the sailor comes first

blocks.note: AB = able seaman
a road is a way, as in highway

annotation.surface: A sailor is on his way to foreign parts.
annotation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adverbs mean in a foreign country.

entries.clue: Mistake to entertain listener not keen on the stock market (7)

definitions.text: not keen on the stock market

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so the listener goes inside the mistake

blocks.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
the ear does the listening; it goes inside BISH

annotation.surface: It is a mistake to amuse a pessimistic investor.
annotation.walkthrough: Bish, a British slang word for a mistake, is the one hard piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A market term: a bear expects prices to fall, so a bearish investor is pessimistic about stocks.

entries.clue: Flash cravat sported by peacekeeping force policeman (7)

indicators.note: a thing sported by someone is worn by them, so the cravat is attached to the force

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a flash
UN = United Nations
a cravat is a kind of tie

annotation.surface: A showy cravat is worn by a policeman in a UN peacekeeping force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flash' reads as an adjective for the cravat; it is a noun meaning a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is one kind of policeman.

entries.clue: Boy wonder exposed witchcraft (3)

indicators.note: something exposed has its covering stripped off, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: Batman's young sidekick; drop the first and last letters

annotation.surface: A child prodigy is revealed to be practising witchcraft.
annotation.walkthrough: The Boy Wonder is Robin in the Batman stories; strip him to OBI.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword staple: obi, or obeah, is a form of sorcery practised in the Caribbean.

entries.clue: Timid girl told fibs about retired vicar (4-7)

indicators.note: about means around, so the fibs go around the vicar
to retire is to draw back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a girl's name
told untruths
REV = Reverend, a vicar; turned back to VER and put inside LIED

annotation.surface: A shy girl lies about an elderly vicar who has stopped working.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired vicar' reads as a pensioner; retired means turned back.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a pale liver was once thought the sign of a coward, so the word means lacking courage.

entries.clue: Pack animal (3)

blocks.note: a verb: to cram in tightly
a male sheep

annotation.walkthrough: 'Pack animal' looks like a mule or donkey; split it into two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: to cram things in hard, and the male of the sheep.

entries.clue: Exciting Sudanese stage performer (8)

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, and stirred letters change places

blocks.note: 8 letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A thrilling performer from Sudan takes the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exciting' reads as praise of the performer; it only tells you to rearrange SUDANESE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a female ballet dancer, French for dancer, is a stage performer.

entries.clue: Paint stiffly formal English king (6)

blocks.note: starchy, proper
ER = Edwardus Rex, King Edward

annotation.surface: A painting of a stiff and stately English king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paint' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the undercoat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the first coat that prepares a surface is one kind of paint.
